providers.d: Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy and Starship from Florida, California and Texas. Webcasts stream on X and spacex.com.
New Glenn from Cape Canaveral and New Shepard suborbital flights from West Texas.
Crew, science and Artemis missions, with launch coverage on NASA+.
Vulcan and Atlas V for national security, NASA and commercial missions.
Electron from Mahia, New Zealand and Wallops Island, Virginia, and the new Neutron rocket.
Minotaur and Pegasus rockets and the Cygnus cargo ship for the space station.
The Alpha small launcher from Vandenberg and the Blue Ghost lunar landers.
Terran R, a reusable medium lift rocket built to fly from Cape Canaveral.
Nova, a fully reusable rocket flying from Cape Canaveral.
Ariane 6 from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana.
Europe's space agency. Live coverage of Ariane 6, Vega C and European science launches.
PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 from Sriharikota, including the Gaganyaan crew program.
H3 launches from Tanegashima, built and flown with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.
Soyuz and Angara launches from Baikonur, Vostochny and Plesetsk.
China's space agency. Long March rockets are built and launched by CASC.

notes: Roscosmos website left out: www.roscosmos.ru answers automated requests with 403 and en.roscosmos.ru (the address Launch Library lists) has an expired certificate.

Roscosmos YouTube and X left out: no official YouTube channel could be found (youtube.com/@roscosmos does not exist), and x.com/roscosmos exists but the Roscosmos site could not be loaded to confirm it is official, so the card has no links.
CNSA YouTube and social pages left out: cnsa.gov.cn links to none, and youtube.com/@CNSA is not an official CNSA channel.
JAXA English site (global.jaxa.jp) left out: it answers automated requests with 403. The Japanese site www.jaxa.jp is used instead; its own links give the YouTube channel and x.com/JAXA_jp.

SpaceX, ISRO and Relativity YouTube channels are not linked in the static HTML of their sites; each channel's own page links back to the official domain (spacex.com, isro.gov.in, relativityspace.com).
SpaceX and ISRO X accounts are not linked in the static HTML of their sites; both were confirmed to exist with X's public embed endpoint.
Every other site, YouTube and X link is linked from the provider's own website and answered 200 to curl.
